question: Can any invertible direct linear block map over F29 turn the first twelve runes of an unsolved LP2 page into one of nine fixed known-reading openings?
field: Canonical GP rune indices 0..28 with arithmetic modulo the prime 29.
input: LP2-00..55, excluding runeless LP2-50; first twelve recognized runes per page including headings; page-local origin zero, no padding or reversal.
blocks: For dimension n in {2,3}, split the first twelve ciphertext and target indices into consecutive n-symbol column vectors. Require a single unknown invertible n by n matrix D with P_j=D C_j for every block j.
cribs: All nine fixed 12-rune vectors in experiments/records/lp2-known-vigenere-keys/plan.json, frozen before this test.
criterion: An exact full-opening fit exists iff all linear dependencies among the ciphertext blocks also hold among the target blocks AND their spans have equal rank. Rank-deficient fits are counted as invertible extensions, not rejected.
extension_count: For common rank r, the number of full invertible n by n extensions is the product over j=r..n-1 of (29^n-29^j); for r=n this is one.
size: 2 dimensions × 55 page starts × 9 fixed openings = 990 complete-key feasibility cases, no matrix brute force.
controls: Independent stacked-rank criterion, planted full-rank and deficient-rank positive cases, inconsistent and zero-input negatives, exhaustive invertible 2x2 and 3x3 matrices over F2 and F3 for small-field oracle cases.
exclusions: Affine constants, alternative block origins or directions, row/column permutations, transposition, padding, other plaintexts, later page positions, cross-page keys and any LP magic-square interpretation.
